diagnosis.root_cause: Q16 hot loop over 8M partsupp rows performs 2 unordered_set::count() hash probes per row for filtering, plus unordered_map lookup + unordered_set::insert per qualifying row (~1.1M rows). These hash operations are cache-hostile with random access patterns, dominating the 630ms runtime.
diagnosis.memory_footprint: unordered_map<Q16Key, unordered_set<int32_t>>: ~1.1M entries across ~18K groups, each unordered_set node-allocated = ~50-100MB random heap allocations

edit_summary: Replaced all hash-based data structures in Q16 partsupp scan with flat array lookups. Pre-classify 2M parts into group_ids via array[partkey]. Hot loop reduced to: array lookup + branch + vector push_back. Count distinct suppkeys via sort-based approach instead of per-group hash sets.
expected_improvement: ~400-500ms reduction in fused_scan_partsupp (from 630ms to ~130-200ms), ~20-25% batch total improvement
